record.paper_title: Initial state fluctuations and final state correlations: Status and open questions
record.original_question: What is the current uncertainty in the viscosity and transport properties of the quark-gluon plasma inferred from anisotropic-flow observables, and what strategy would best reduce that uncertainty?

evidence.quote:
• What is the current uncertainty in the viscosity of the QGP, and what is the best
strategy for reducing it?

Some questions arose as to how a meaningful comparison to theory calculations can
and should be performed, which is crucial for any quantitative statements about the
transport coefficients of the quark gluon plasma.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a hot, deconfined state of strongly interacting matter (a quark–gluon plasma) produced in relativistic heavy-ion collisions, modeled as a nearly perfect relativistic fluid characterized by a temperature-dependent specific shear viscosity η/s(T) and specific bulk viscosity ζ/s(T). The azimuthal anisotropy of produced hadrons is encoded in the Fourier coefficients v_n (n = 2, 3, 4, …) of the single-particle distribution and in their event-by-event fluctuations and correlations, which are sensitive to the transport coefficients of the fluid as well as to the fluctuating initial conditions, the equation of state, and the particlization/hadronic-rescattering stage.

(a) Quantify the current uncertainty (e.g., a credible interval as a function of T) on η/s(T) and ζ/s(T) of the quark–gluon plasma when these functions are inferred from measured anisotropic-flow observables {v_n} (including their event-by-event fluctuations and multi-particle cumulants) via a global model-to-data comparison.

(b) Determine an optimal strategy for reducing this uncertainty, specifying which combinations of flow observables, collision systems and energies, and which improvements in the modeling of the initial state, the hydrodynamic evolution, and the late-stage hadronic dynamics most efficiently constrain η/s(T) and ζ/s(T).
artifact.status_search_result: Bayesian global analyses combining viscous relativistic hydrodynamics with measured anisotropic flow have produced increasingly precise posterior distributions for η/s(T) and ζ/s(T), with current relative precision on (η/s) reported at roughly the 5–10% level in some studies. The problem is therefore actively being addressed and partially solved, but a fully agreed-upon uncertainty and an optimal reduction strategy remain under investigation, with ongoing work on initial-state modeling, particlization, and finite-μ_B extensions.

status_evidence.title: Bayesian estimation of the specific shear and bulk viscosity of quark–gluon plasma
status_evidence.snippet: Bayesian parameter estimation provides a reliable estimation of the temperature-dependent specific shear and bulk viscosities of QGP.
status_evidence.claim: Bayesian inference yields temperature-dependent posteriors for η/s(T) and ζ/s(T), giving quantitative but model-dependent uncertainty bands.

status_evidence.title: The road to precision: Extraction of the specific shear viscosity of the QGP
status_evidence.snippet: Phenomenological extraction of (η/s)QGP with a relative precision of order 5-10% now appears within reach through access to the full spectrum of vn and their event-by-event fluctuations.
status_evidence.claim: Strategy involves using full vn spectrum and event-by-event fluctuations; ~5–10% precision considered achievable.

status_evidence.title: Transport Properties of QGP within a Bayesian Holographic QCD Model
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work uses Bayesian holographic QCD modeling to constrain QGP transport coefficients, including at finite baryon density.
status_evidence.claim: Active 2024–2025 work continues to refine viscosity uncertainties using Bayesian methods.
